selection_policy.notes: Selected to balance accept/reject decisions while spreading across representative source cases.

planning_patterns.proposed_change: Add a Reactor location node and link it to the retained low-pressure condition with a has edge.
planning_patterns.matched_rule: Add a supporting entity node when a retained condition is explicitly described as belonging to specific equipment and otherwise lacks a valid incoming characterization link.
planning_patterns.few_shot_takeaway: If a condition is kept but its owning equipment is missing, accept the smallest evidence-grounded entity addition that anchors that condition.

planning_patterns.proposed_change: Delete redundant location node 'overhead vapor line'.
planning_patterns.matched_rule: Remove standalone location nodes when the same local mechanism is already captured by retained event nodes.
planning_patterns.few_shot_takeaway: If a location adds no independent causal role beyond a retained event, delete the location node rather than keeping duplicate structure.

planning_patterns.proposed_change: Add an enables edge from the liquid-phase condition to the event where liquid methyl mercaptan entered the waste gas vent header.
planning_patterns.matched_rule: Retained local conditions should be linked to the specific event they directly enable.
planning_patterns.few_shot_takeaway: When a kept condition is explicitly the local state behind a nearby event, add the direct condition-to-event link rather than leaving the condition structurally idle.

planning_patterns.proposed_change: Add a material-to-temperature edge from the solvent mixture to the high-temperature condition.
planning_patterns.matched_rule: Add a local entity-to-condition link when a retained state node lacks attachment to the material it describes.
planning_patterns.few_shot_takeaway: If a retained condition is causally used but locally unattached, add the missing descriptive link.

planning_patterns.proposed_change: Rename the dust-lofting event so it represents only post-primary-explosion dispersion, not the primary explosion itself.
planning_patterns.matched_rule: When one event node merges an initiating explosion with a later dispersion stage, separate the stages so each local mechanism is represented distinctly.
planning_patterns.few_shot_takeaway: If an event name mixes event occurrence and later propagation, narrow the existing node to one stage and leave the other stage to a separate node.

planning_patterns.proposed_change: Add edge Ev6 -> H1 (enables) from large vapor cloud formation to flash fire.
planning_patterns.matched_rule: When the dispersed flammable cloud is the combustible body involved in the fire, add a direct local link from the cloud node to the fire consequence rather than routing that contribution only through an ignition-source node.
planning_patterns.few_shot_takeaway: Accept direct cloud-to-fire links when the cloud itself is the burning hazard in the final consequence.

planning_patterns.matched_rule: Do not remove a node for redundancy based only on semantic overlap across different node types; remove only truly descriptive-only nodes with no needed causal role.
planning_patterns.few_shot_takeaway: Reject node deletions when the redundancy claim depends mainly on cross-type similarity rather than clear structural nonuse.

planning_patterns.proposed_change: Delete the condition node "Liquid" as a redundant descriptive state.
planning_patterns.matched_rule: Do not delete a typed node as redundant solely because similar context is expressed by a different node type.
planning_patterns.few_shot_takeaway: Reject redundancy deletions that rely only on cross-type semantic overlap.

planning_patterns.reviewer_reason: don't identify redundancy accross different types
planning_patterns.matched_rule: Do not apply redundancy deletion when the claim depends only on cross-type overlap rather than true duplicate semantics.
planning_patterns.few_shot_takeaway: Do not delete a condition node just because it looks descriptively similar to another node of a different type.

planning_patterns.reviewer_reason: The phase sould be identified as it is better for people to understand the phase of the released material
planning_patterns.matched_rule: Do not delete a material-condition descriptor when reviewers judge it necessary for understanding the released material, even if its direct causal role is limited.
planning_patterns.few_shot_takeaway: Do not remove phase information when it is needed as explanatory context for interpreting the material involved.

planning_patterns.proposed_change: Delete the liquid-phase condition node as redundant.
planning_patterns.matched_rule: Do not delete a condition node solely because an event elsewhere expresses related semantics; cross-type overlap alone is not valid redundancy.
planning_patterns.few_shot_takeaway: Do not remove a condition node just because an event mentions the same state; redundancy must be shown within the same semantic role.

planning_patterns.reviewer_reason: Redundancy cannot be identified accross different types
planning_patterns.matched_rule: Do not remove a condition as redundant solely because a related event exists; redundancy requires no independent local causal role, and cross-type semantics are not automatically duplicates.
planning_patterns.few_shot_takeaway: Before deleting a state node for redundancy, confirm true functional duplication rather than overlap with an event of a different type.

diagnosis_patterns.observed_pattern: A retained equipment-specific condition was left unanchored.
diagnosis_patterns.diagnosis_interpretation: The issue should be framed as structural incompleteness in condition anchoring, not as a missing causal step in the main pathway.
diagnosis_patterns.supporting_rule: When a report describes a condition as specific to named equipment, diagnosis should treat the missing equipment entity as needed support for that retained condition.
diagnosis_patterns.few_shot_takeaway: Diagnose missing owner entities for retained conditions as anchoring gaps that should be fixed without expanding the causal sequence.

diagnosis_patterns.observed_pattern: Standalone location duplicates an event-local mechanism.
diagnosis_patterns.diagnosis_interpretation: The diagnosis treats local equipment context as redundant when the same role is already embedded in a retained event description.
diagnosis_patterns.supporting_rule: Separate location nodes are redundant when the same local mechanism is already expressed directly by event nodes.
diagnosis_patterns.few_shot_takeaway: Diagnose redundant structure when a location node only restates where an already-retained event occurs.

diagnosis_patterns.observed_pattern: A retained phase condition lacked a downstream link to the event it locally conditions.
diagnosis_patterns.diagnosis_interpretation: This should be diagnosed as a missing local causal link, not as harmless extra detail, when the retained state directly enables a specific nearby event.
diagnosis_patterns.supporting_rule: Retained local conditions should connect to the event they directly enable.
diagnosis_patterns.few_shot_takeaway: Diagnose unlinked but relevant local states as missing-link problems when they have an explicit event-level role.

diagnosis_patterns.observed_pattern: A retained temperature condition was causally active but unattached to its material.
diagnosis_patterns.diagnosis_interpretation: This should be diagnosed as a missing local descriptive link in state attribution, not as a gap in the main accident pathway.
diagnosis_patterns.supporting_rule: A retained material condition that enables an event should still be linked to the material whose state it describes.
diagnosis_patterns.few_shot_takeaway: Diagnose unattached retained condition nodes as local-link omissions.

diagnosis_patterns.observed_pattern: One event node mixes the primary event with a later dispersion stage.
diagnosis_patterns.diagnosis_interpretation: This should be diagnosed as an over-merged local mechanism, with the downstream node framed as the later dispersion step only.
diagnosis_patterns.supporting_rule: If a node compresses two distinct local stages, diagnose it as over-merged rather than leaving the mechanism implicit.
diagnosis_patterns.few_shot_takeaway: Flag over-merged nodes when they collapse event occurrence and later propagation into a single step.

diagnosis_patterns.observed_pattern: A dispersed combustible cloud is linked directly to the fire consequence.
diagnosis_patterns.diagnosis_interpretation: The final-stage issue should be diagnosed as a missing local consequence link from the combustible cloud to the fire, not only as an ignition-source modeling problem.
diagnosis_patterns.supporting_rule: Missing local links should be added when the combustible cloud directly participates in the hazard consequence.
diagnosis_patterns.few_shot_takeaway: Diagnose flash-fire structure by checking whether the fuel cloud itself connects directly to the fire consequence.

diagnosis_patterns.observed_pattern: A condition appears semantically similar to content already represented by another node type.
diagnosis_patterns.diagnosis_interpretation: Reviewer treated cross-type similarity as insufficient for a redundancy diagnosis. Redundancy should be framed structurally, not just semantically.
diagnosis_patterns.supporting_rule: Diagnose redundancy only for nodes that are descriptive-only and lack a necessary causal role.
diagnosis_patterns.few_shot_takeaway: Do not diagnose a node as redundant solely because an event, entity, and condition express related ideas.

diagnosis_patterns.observed_pattern: A condition node overlaps descriptively with event or material context across node types.
diagnosis_patterns.diagnosis_interpretation: Cross-type overlap alone is not sufficient grounds to diagnose the condition as redundant.
diagnosis_patterns.supporting_rule: Redundancy should be diagnosed from lack of distinct causal role, not merely from semantic similarity across node types.
diagnosis_patterns.few_shot_takeaway: Only diagnose redundancy when a node adds no distinct typed causal information.

diagnosis_patterns.observed_pattern: A descriptive condition was kept despite a prior redundant-node diagnosis.
diagnosis_patterns.diagnosis_interpretation: The review implies the redundancy framing was too aggressive because it treated different semantic types as interchangeable duplicates.
diagnosis_patterns.supporting_rule: Do not diagnose redundancy across different semantic types unless there is true duplicate meaning and no distinct role.
diagnosis_patterns.few_shot_takeaway: Do not label a node redundant solely because it overlaps descriptively with a node of another type.

diagnosis_patterns.observed_pattern: Material phase descriptor retained for interpretive value.
diagnosis_patterns.diagnosis_interpretation: The reviewer treated phase as meaningful explanatory context, so the issue should not be framed as automatic redundancy just because the node originally appeared weakly integrated.
diagnosis_patterns.supporting_rule: A descriptor should only be diagnosed as redundant when it lacks a needed supported role; if it is needed to interpret the material involved, keep it in scope.
diagnosis_patterns.few_shot_takeaway: Be cautious diagnosing phase or property nodes as redundant when they help users understand the released material.

diagnosis_patterns.observed_pattern: A condition node shared content with an event node but belonged to a different node type.
diagnosis_patterns.diagnosis_interpretation: Redundancy should not be diagnosed from cross-type semantic similarity alone; conditions and events may carry distinct structural meaning even when they describe related states.
diagnosis_patterns.supporting_rule: Do not diagnose redundancy across different node types without showing that one node fully replaces the other's pathway role.
diagnosis_patterns.few_shot_takeaway: Be cautious diagnosing redundancy across node types; similar wording is not enough.

diagnosis_patterns.observed_pattern: An upstream phase condition was kept despite overlap with a related event.
diagnosis_patterns.diagnosis_interpretation: The issue should not be framed as simple redundancy when a condition and an event are different semantic types and duplicate function has not been shown.
diagnosis_patterns.supporting_rule: Redundancy should be diagnosed only when a node lacks an independent local causal role, not merely because a nearby event expresses related meaning.
diagnosis_patterns.few_shot_takeaway: Diagnose redundancy by functional duplication, not by condition-event similarity alone.

coverage_notes: Acceptance of node_deletion_1 structurally covered edge_deletion_1, since removing C2 required removing its incident En1 -> C2 edge.
Acceptance of the En2->En3 edge deletion was implicitly covered by acceptance of deleting both endpoint nodes.
Acceptance of the vapor cloud-to-VCE edge and deletion of the cloud-to-ignition edge jointly reframe the ignition stage so the cloud and ignition source act as separate contributors to the explosion.
Acceptance of the vapor-phase node deletion implicitly covered deletion of its only descriptive edge.
Acceptance of the vapor-phase node deletion implicitly supports cleanup of its attached material-to-phase edge, which was separately accepted.

After the rejection of the solid-phase node deletion, the updated graph kept that node and added an extra anchor edge from the material to the solid condition, indicating preservation rather than redundancy treatment.
Both rejected edge deletions were implicitly covered by the rejection of the paired node deletions; the updated graph retains the original has-edges because the target nodes were kept.
No separate edge-review decisions were needed because the needed has edges were covered as part of the accepted node additions.

Rejection of node_deletion_2 also explains rejection of edge_deletion_2; the updated graph further reinforced C4 retention by adding a downstream causal link from High confinement to nitrogen accumulation.
Rejection of the En1->C1 edge deletion directly followed from rejection of deleting C1.
Rejection of the liquid-phase node deletion also explains rejection of deleting its attached material-state edge; the edge remains valid because the node was retained.
Rejection of the liquid-phase node deletion also implied rejection of deleting its supporting descriptive edge.
The accepted deletion of the drain-valve location also implicitly covered removal of its containment edge from the vent header; that edge deletion did not require a separate reviewed suggestion.

The accepted deletions and accepted vapor-cloud-to-fire addition consistently reframe the final fire stage away from 'fuel causes ignition source' and toward 'fuel conditions contribute directly to the hazard consequence.'
The accepted hydrocarbon-air mixture node addition was implemented in the updated graph as En7 plus the implicit characterization edge En7 -> C3.
The accepted material-to-temperature edge addition repaired the retained high-temperature condition after the phase-node review split outcome.

unresolved_decisions.note: Planned deletion of edge raffinate splitter tower -> overhead vapor line has no explicit review_decisions entry, but it appears in deleted_edges and is absent from the updated graph, suggesting implicit coverage.

The planned addition of C2 -> H1 (enables) has no explicit review decision. A related C2 -> H1 edge appears in the updated graph, but with relation 'has' rather than the proposed 'enables', so the reviewed outcome cannot be matched exactly.
The planned combustibility-to-consequence edge has no explicit review decision in the review state and was not implemented in the updated graph.

planning.takeaway: Reject redundancy deletions that rely only on cross-type semantic overlap.
Reject dependent edge deletions if the related node deletion was not accepted.
If a condition is kept but its owning equipment is missing, accept the smallest evidence-grounded entity addition that anchors that condition.
If a combustible condition is retained without a represented material, accept a material-node addition that anchors the condition to the identified hazardous mixture.
When a kept condition is explicitly the local state behind a nearby event, add the direct condition-to-event link rather than leaving the condition structurally idle.
If a retained condition describes a material or system state, attach it to that entity so the condition is not left unanchored.
Anchor retained operating-state conditions to the equipment or location they belong to instead of leaving them free-standing.
Before deleting a node for redundancy, check whether the overlap is truly same-role duplication rather than cross-type restatement.
A component/location node can be removed when nearby retained events already capture its only function in the accident sequence.
If a location adds no independent causal role beyond a retained event, delete the location node rather than keeping duplicate structure.

diagnosis.takeaway: Diagnose missing owner entities for retained conditions as anchoring gaps that should be fixed without expanding the causal sequence.
Diagnose missing material anchors for retained hazard properties as support-node omissions rather than as missing downstream consequence logic.
Diagnose unlinked but relevant local states as missing-link problems when they have an explicit event-level role.
When a kept condition floats without an owning entity, diagnose anchoring incompleteness first.
Diagnose standalone operating-state nodes as incomplete unless they are tied to the equipment or location whose state they express.
Diagnose redundancy only when two nodes duplicate the same causal role, not merely the same subject matter.
If a component node only repeats where an already-retained action happened, diagnose it as redundant rather than essential structure.
Diagnose redundant structure when a location node only restates where an already-retained event occurs.
Treat separate location nodes as redundant when event nodes already carry the local causal meaning.
Diagnose ungrounded condition nodes as a completeness problem, especially for equipment states like pressure or temperature.

planning_matched_rules.rule: Remove standalone location nodes when the same local mechanism is already captured by retained event nodes.
Retained condition nodes should be attached to the equipment state they characterize.
Do not delete a typed node as redundant solely because similar context is expressed by a different node type.
Do not remove an edge when its only deletion rationale was cleanup for a node that remains in the graph.
Add a supporting entity node when a retained condition is explicitly described as belonging to specific equipment and otherwise lacks a valid incoming characterization link.
Add a supporting material node when a retained combustibility condition is explicitly tied to a specific hazardous mixture and otherwise lacks a valid incoming characterization link.
Retained local conditions should be linked to the specific event they directly enable.
Retained condition nodes should be anchored by an incoming entity-state link to the material or system they characterize.
Retained pressure or state conditions should be attached to the location or equipment they characterize.
Do not treat semantic overlap across different node types as automatic redundancy when the nodes may represent different causal roles.
Remove a node when its semantics are already fully carried by retained event nodes and it adds no independent causal role.
Retained condition nodes should connect to the local release stage they directly enable.

diagnosis_supporting_rules.rule: Separate location nodes are redundant when the same local mechanism is already expressed directly by event nodes.
Retained condition nodes are structurally incomplete if they are not fully linked to the equipment they characterize.
Redundancy should be diagnosed from lack of distinct causal role, not merely from semantic similarity across node types.
Remove support edges only when the node they only serve is actually removed.
When a report describes a condition as specific to named equipment, diagnosis should treat the missing equipment entity as needed support for that retained condition.
When a report identifies a specific flammable mixture, diagnosis should treat the missing material entity as required support for any retained combustibility condition.
Retained local conditions should connect to the event they directly enable.
Retained condition nodes should be anchored to the material or system they characterize.
Pressure or operating-state conditions should be attached to the equipment or location they characterize.
Do not diagnose redundancy solely from overlap across different node types.
A node is diagnostically redundant when retained events already capture its entire causal contribution.
Retained condition nodes are structurally incomplete if they are not fully linked to the mechanisms they describe.
